positions.commentary: EA's business is hit-driven, and while it can be interesting from an investment perspective, things can come out of nowhere and do extremely well.

thesis: This episode argues that EA is a superior acquisition target and investment compared to Take-Two due to its stable recurring revenue, successful studio consolidation, and strategic mobile presence. It posits that EA has evolved from a hit-driven business into a SaaS-like model with predictable earnings, making it a smart operator that reinvests in content creation.

claims.claim: EA is a potential acquisition target for companies like Amazon or Comcast due to its strategic value in the interactive space.
claims.quote: And the strategic benefit to those buyers, I think with Microsoft Activision, I know it hasn't necessarily been for the strategy, which you would initially think in terms of the Xbox and maybe holding games hostage, it's quite the opposite.

claims.claim: EA's content is mostly licensed, making it harder to acquire compared to Take-Two.
claims.quote: EA is a little bit different in the sense that majority of their content is licensed, most of their biggest content, so it's a little bit harder.

claims.claim: EA has stable earnings and trades at an ongoing multiple, unlike Take-Two which is hit-driven.
claims.quote: On the flip side, Activision, and EA kind of have much more stable earnings. And so they traded an ongoing multiple. And I think that makes the most sense.

claims.claim: EA has grown FIFA over the last decade, maintaining a core group of loyal spenders.
claims.quote: EA has grown FIFA over the last decade every year, some higher than others, but it's still like this ongoing business. They have this core group of people that are continuing to spend and have complete loyalty.

claims.claim: EA's CEO generally hates mobile, similar to Take-Two's Strauss.
claims.quote: similar to the way EA, the CEO of EA, hates mobile, generally speaking. So anyway, I think he was kind of pressured into building it.

claims.claim: EA's mobile presence is significant, making it a strategic pillar for any company.
claims.quote: Both of which have mobile. This was a way of almost overnight getting into mobile, but it was just the wrong acquisition at the wrong time.

claims.claim: EA is viewed as a smart operator that successfully reinvested in building new AAA game teams and studios, unlike Take Two.
claims.quote: EA did the smart thing. They bought respawn, right? And they bought that management team and that group. And Vincent Bell, he's an amazing operator and studio leader, which is the hardest roles to fill within these type of organizations.

claims.claim: EA has created multiple successful studios under Vincent Bell that are producing high-quality AAA content like Star Wars and Black Panther games.
claims.quote: And he's created like four or five studios under him that are actually creating AAA content, including the Star Wars game, including the Black Panther game and the Iron Man game.

claims.claim: EA is seen as a smart publisher that consolidated to fewer franchises and focused on revenue per user, similar to the broader industry trend.
claims.quote: Historically, when I was the first at EA, we were building like 30 games a year. Now, if they do six games, that's a lot. And again, the focus has been on revenue per user as opposed to tons of games trying to expand the audience.

claims.claim: EA is viewed as a smart operator that reinvested revenue into building teams to build more content, unlike Take Two which lacks the capability.
claims.quote: EA has been really smart in reinvesting some of their revenue and earnings into building out these teams to build more content, right? They just don't have the capability that I see within Take 2 to actually do anything.

claims.claim: EA has successfully grown FIFA into a predictable ongoing business with a loyal core group of people continuing to spend.
claims.quote: EA has grown FIFA over the last decade every year, some higher than others, but it's still like this ongoing business. They have this core group of people that are continuing to spend and have complete loyalty.

claims.claim: EA's multiple has expanded significantly due to the evolution of in-game purchases, moving from a lower hit-driven business to a SaaS-like model.
claims.quote: Historically, the multiple was a lot lower because of the hits-driven business. But now that they are kind of a SaaS business to some degree, their multiple multiple definitely expanded to the 20 to 25 range.
